noHostServing: no wsp host is serving {state}; start one with wsp up --state {state}
hostTokenMissing: the host's token file is missing: {path}
noAnswer: the host at {where} did not answer: {why}
noAnswerWithin: the host at {where} did not answer: nothing came back within {ms} ms
hostStopping: the host is restarting; the turn goes on and its reply lands in the thread
noSuchHostNone: no host named {alias} is connected; this computer holds none, and wsp login puts the hosts on your account here. Run wsp hosts for the list.
noSuchHostSome: no host named {alias} is connected; this computer holds {known}, and wsp login puts the hosts on your account here. Run wsp hosts for the list.
severalHosts:
this computer can reach {count} hosts on your account ({aliases}) and none of them is the one every line takes. Name one on the line with --host <name>.

Run wsp hosts for the list.
addressNotPaired: --host takes the name of a host on your account; {url} is an address, and wsp hosts lists the names. Run wsp hosts for the list.
hostNoKey: {where} names a host and no key for it, so this computer cannot tell which host it would be sending its token to; run wsp hosts to read the account's hosts again
launchedWith: the launch this turn started with
deviceRefused: the host {alias} refused this computer's token, which it has taken away; run wsp logout, wsp login and wsp hosts to sign this computer in again.
scopedNoPair: this thread's tools were launched without its own host token, so they refuse rather than act as the person; the agent did not pass WSP_HOST_URL and WSP_HOST_TOKEN to its MCP server
startingHost: starting the host for {state}; its log is {log}, and wsp down stops it
hostExited: the host for {state} exited with {ended} before it served; its log is {log}

agentNames.build-essential: C toolchain with cmake and ninja

otherVersion: the host answered {op} in a shape this wsp does not read; it runs another version of wsp, restart it with wsp up
aimedUsage: {tool} takes a workspace or on, not both
aimedBoth: A workspace already names its computer; give the workspace or --on <computer>, not both. {usage}
projectUnnamed: --project with --on names the project: --project <name>, as wsp projects shows it. {usage}
projectOffComputer: --project {value} names a project on a computer, which --on names; a workspace's own project is --project alone. {usage}
toolsProjectBare: --project on wsp servers tools names a project on --on <computer>; a workspace finds its own project's servers. {usage}
skillsShPlaceless: {skill} is read off skills.sh, which names no computer or project. {usage}
unsetVariable: {variable} is not set in this environment, so there is no value to write. {usage}
unclosedQuote: The command has a quote it never closes, so nothing was written. {usage}
projectScope: --project is the project scope, not {scope}; give one of the two. {usage}
